messages:
alex: paging: we've got elevated tail p99 on the continuous-batching path in us-west-2, started ~15:10 UTC, p95 ~450ms -> 900ms, p99 spiking to 6-8s for streaming RPCs. customer-facing errors not widespread yet but a few customers reported timeouts. incident-bot: incident created INC-2026-8452. alex: @maria @jamal can you ack?
maria: acked. oncall taking. just pulled grafana traces — looks correlated with mixed-seqlen batches where a single long seq sits in the pack and stalls streaming consumers.
jamal: also seeing sudden increase in pack size variance, `pack_size_stddev` jumped from 1.2 -> 4.9 around 15:09. logs attached show repeated preempt events + KV cache churn.
kim: tagging in SRE for paging handoff. kim: customer-impact: two high-usage customers (cust-phi & cust-neo) saw >10% of requests hit >3s, support ticket open.
sre-bot: oncall whoami -> jamal listed as primary. ops-bot: escalations: notif sent to infra-leads.
jamal: immediate plan: 1) switch continuous-batcher to conservative packing (max_batch_size=64 -> 32) 2) enable pack-timeout=30ms -> 10ms to reduce waiting for long sequences 3) short-circuit streaming hedging to fallback model variant if stall >1s. anyone object?
maria: +1 for reducing max_batch_size. hedging maybe risky for quality; prefer reducing pack timeout first then hedging if no improvement.
alex: do the config changes as a canary on a small fleet first (us-west-2a). jamal do you want me to kick the deploy?
jamal: I'm on it. pushing canary config now:
```
# canary config
continuous_batcher:
  max_batch_size: 32
  pack_timeout_ms: 10
  hetero_pack_enabled: false
  scheduler_weight_adjust: true
```

jamal: applying via infra-config-reloader -> `kubectl rollout restart deploy/continuous-batcher-canary -n inference-usw2a`
kim: I'll monitor customer-facing SLO dashboards and support queue. setting a short customer notify draft.
maria: quick metric checks: running `curl -s "https://metrics.prod/grafana/api/datasources/proxy/1/api/ds/query" -d '{query:"sum(rate(streaming_latency_bucket[1m])) by (le)"}'` to validate tail bucket change (will paste results).
alex: can we also adjust scheduler to prefer smaller packs when stream flag set? set `fair_share_prefer_small=true` on canary scheduler config.
jamal: canary deployed 15:22 UTC. initial telemetry: p95 dropped to ~380ms at 15:28, p99 down to ~1.2s (huge improvement) but still occasional spikes ~2.5s.
kim: support reports timeouts reduced for cust-neo, cust-phi still seeing occasional 4s tails.
maria: digging traces — those remaining spikes are correlated with requests that include a 10k token prompt (edge-case) which still forces single-request huge pack. we can add an additional pre-filter: if seq_len>4k route to dedicated small-queue that uses greedy-pack=false.
ajamal: typo — jamal here: creating route rule now, will add rule id rr-2026-74, non-disruptive.
jamal: rr-2026-74 pushed to canary, routes seq_len>4096 to per-request path (no batching).
jamal: after route push p99 stabilized ~900ms at 15:38. pack timeout change reduced latency variance.
kim: good. next steps: 1) run a 1h canary verification 2) if steady, roll to region 2 (us-west-2b) then us-east-1 3) prepare postmortem note and customer communication for affected tenants.
alex: who's owning postmortem? I can draft initial timeline. jamal can you collect packing histograms and attach config diffs. maria to own customer-facing note with support.
maria: will draft customer note: emphasize mitigations, ETA for full rollouts, and temporary workaround (rate-limit long prompts or route to dedicated).
ajamal: attaching sparse logs: `batcher_pack_queue_depth` + `pack_timeout_ms` traces exported to /tmp/pack-hist-1911112222.log (internal link).
kim: anyone want to escalate to infra for kernel-level perf? not yet — metrics look config-level. if another spike after rollouts we escalate.
sre-bot: reminder: update incident INC-2026-8452 with canary results and next rollout windows.
alex: agreed. thanks team. will keep thread open until rollouts complete and SLOs steady for 1h. :thumbsup:
